title: MATH GAOKAO - 387
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by \(3\) using the sum of its digits.
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(3\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(3\) if the sum of its digits is divisible by \(3\). For \(12345\), the digit sum is \(1+2+3+4+5=15\), and \(15\) is divisible by \(3\). For \(12347\), the digit sum is \(1+2+3+4+7=17\), which is not divisible by \(3\). Therefore, \(12345\) is divisible by \(3\), so the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Add the digits of each number and check whether the sum is a multiple of \(3\).

questions.learningObjective: Apply the last-two-digits rule to determine divisibility by \(4\).
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(4\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(4\) if its last two digits form a number divisible by \(4\). For \(1234\), the last two digits are \(34\), and \(34\) is not divisible by \(4\). For \(1236\), the last two digits are \(36\), and \(36=4\cdot 9\), so \(36\) is divisible by \(4\). Therefore, \(1236\) is divisible by \(4\), so the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Check only the last two digits of each number.

questions.learningObjective: Determine divisibility by \(9\) using the sum of digits.
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(9\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(9\) if the sum of its digits is divisible by \(9\). For \(2356\), the digit sum is \(2+3+5+6=16\), which is not divisible by \(9\). For \(2358\), the digit sum is \(2+3+5+8=18\), and \(18\) is divisible by \(9\). Therefore, \(2358\) is divisible by \(9\), so the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Use the digit-sum rule for divisibility by \(9\).

questions.learningObjective: Find a missing digit in a four-digit number divisible by \(11\).
questions.question: The four-digit number \(\overline{3a74}\) is divisible by \(11\), where \(a\) is a digit. What is the value of \(a\)?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by \(11\), the alternating sum of the digits must be divisible by \(11\). For \(\overline{3a74}\), the alternating sum is \((3+7)-(a+4)=10-a-4=6-a\). Since \(a\) is a digit, the only value that makes \(6-a\) divisible by \(11\) is \(a=6\), giving \(6-6=0\). Thus the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Use the divisibility rule for \(11\): the difference between the sums of digits in alternating positions must be a multiple of \(11\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a number is divisible by \(6\) using divisibility by \(2\) and \(3\).
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(6\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(6\) if it is divisible by both \(2\) and \(3\). For \(2316\), the number is even, so it is divisible by \(2\). Its digit sum is \(2+3+1+6=12\), which is divisible by \(3\), so \(2316\) is divisible by \(6\). For \(2318\), the number is even, but its digit sum is \(2+3+1+8=14\), which is not divisible by \(3\). Therefore, the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Check divisibility by \(2\) and by \(3\) separately.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the last-three-digits rule to test divisibility by \(8\).
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(8\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(8\) if its last three digits form a number divisible by \(8\). For \(5432\), the last three digits are \(432\), and \(432=8\cdot 54\), so \(432\) is divisible by \(8\). For \(5436\), the last three digits are \(436\), and \(436\) is not divisible by \(8\). Therefore, \(5432\) is divisible by \(8\), so the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Check only the last three digits of each number.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a number divisible by \(7\) from a pair of candidates.
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(7\)?
questions.explanation: Divide each number by \(7\). For \(1234\), we have \(1234=7\cdot 176+2\), so the remainder is \(2\), and \(1234\) is not divisible by \(7\). For \(1239\), we have \(1239=7\cdot 177\), so \(1239\) is divisible by \(7\). Therefore, the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Try dividing each number by \(7\), or use a divisibility test for \(7\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the last-two-digits rule to identify a number divisible by \(25\).
questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by \(25\)?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by \(25\) if its last two digits form a number divisible by \(25\). The possible last two digits are \(00\), \(25\), \(50\), or \(75\). For \(1230\), the last two digits are \(30\), which is not divisible by \(25\). For \(1225\), the last two digits are \(25\), which is divisible by \(25\). Therefore, \(1225\) is divisible by \(25\), so the correct choice is B.
questions.hint: Check the last two digits and recall which endings make a number divisible by \(25\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing digit in a four-digit number divisible by \(11\).
questions.question: The four-digit number \(\overline{5a32}\) is divisible by \(11\), where \(a\) is a digit. What is the value of \(a\)?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by \(11\), the alternating sum of the digits must be divisible by \(11\). For \(\overline{5a32}\), the alternating sum is \((5+3)-(a+2)=8-a-2=6-a\). Since \(a\) is a digit, the only value that makes \(6-a\) divisible by \(11\) is \(a=6\), giving \(6-6=0\). Thus the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Apply the alternating-sum rule for divisibility by \(11\).

questions.learningObjective: Use the divisibility rule for \(11\) to find a remainder.
questions.question: What is the remainder when \(123456\) is divided by \(11\)?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by \(11\), compute the alternating sum of the digits from right to left. The digits from the right are \(6,5,4,3,2,1\). The sum of digits in odd positions is \(6+4+2=12\), and the sum of digits in even positions is \(5+3+1=9\). The difference is \(12-9=3\). The original number is congruent to this alternating sum modulo \(11\). Since \(0\le3<11\), its remainder is \(3\). Thus the correct choice is A.
questions.hint: Use the alternating digit sum rule for divisibility by \(11\), then interpret the result as a remainder.
